chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a part of his wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A part is one of ten.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Place on each of them a part on every mountain' — and the mountains were ten.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of 'a part' (juz') when bequeathing wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the indefinite term 'part' (juz') in bequests refers specifically to one-tenth, grounding the legal ruling in Quranic linguistic precedent. By citing the verse where ten mountains were assigned parts, the Imam demonstrates how Quranic usage informs fiqh principles, a methodological approach emphasized by Shia jurists to ensure textual fidelity. This interpretation resolves ambiguity in inheritance law, ensuring that bequests do not exceed the permissible one-third limit while providing clear quantitative standards for testators.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Fazaal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said about a man who bequeathed (donated) with a part from his wealth. Heasws said: ‘A part is a tenth. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [2:260] then place on every mountain a part of them – and the mountains were ten (in number)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Faddal from Th’alabah’ ibn Maymun from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who made a will about a part of his legacy. He (the Imam) said, ‘Apart is one-tenth because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, ‘Place a part on every mountain’ the mountains were ten.’”
